what_is_strong: Every named mechanic in this audit is explicitly registered. There is no gap where Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Imbue, Rewind, Herald, or Shatter fall through to unnamed fallback handling.
The support model is honest and operator-readable: `direct`, `identity_gated_direct`, `partial`, and `warning_only` are separated cleanly instead of overstating runtime competence.

Target behavior is not flattened into vague value rows. Source-backed targeting can lower through `BeforeBattlecryTargetBonus`, while generic spell targeting remains visible as `generic_spell_target` warning-only.

Discover and Choose One are handled conservatively. Exact option identity can lower to `OnDiscoverCardBonus` or `OnChooseOneCardBonus`, and unresolved option identity is suppressed instead of guessed.

Hero Power transforms are explicitly modeled through `hero_power_transform`, with a documented route to `BeforeUseHeroPowerBonus` and supporting static semantic coverage for Start of Game Shadowform-style cards.

Locations, Secrets, generated entities, and aura effects are not hidden. HSConfig represents the lowerable part while keeping repeated activation, secret timing, random pools, and continuous board-state math inside visible warning boundaries.
The no-block contract is consistent across code, tests, and operator docs. A valid deck package can remain load-safe even when some semantics are partial or warning-only.
what_is_not_optimal: Choose One is registered as `support_level=direct` in the registry, but its actual lowering policy is identity-gated with no generic default runtime block. The operator bucket communicates this correctly, but the raw support label alone can be misread if viewed in isolation.

Target behavior coverage is asymmetric by design. Battlecry-target and explicit targeting claims lower well, but generic spell-target selection remains report-only and therefore cannot express the full targeting space of Destroy, Silence, Transform, or Freeze cards.
Locations and Secrets are only partially represented. Play timing is lowerable, but repeated location activation, hidden-information sequencing, and exact trap timing remain warning-only.
Generated entities are only partially represented. Exact resolved identity can lower, but random generation pools remain report-only, which limits pre-run richness for highly stochastic cards.

Several modern or future-facing mechanics remain visibility-only: Dredge, Tradeable, Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Rewind, Herald, Shatter, and truly unknown future mechanics do not have first-class runtime action surfaces.

The strongest proof is registry and unit-test based. The representative deck matrix proves the no-block contract, but it is thinner as a deck-fixture proof set for Secret-heavy, Location-heavy, Dredge, Tradeable, and newer warning-only mechanics.
no_block_assessment: The current skill does avoid blocking valid decks for the requested mechanic set. The decisive contract is structural package validity plus `runtime_apply_mode=load_safe_apply`, not full strategic lowering for every mechanic.
Direct mechanics such as Battlecry, Weapons, and Discard can emit meaningful runtime rows today, so these are not just visible labels.

Identity-gated mechanics such as Discover, Choose One, and Hero Power transforms do not block the package when identity is unresolved; the runtime rows are simply suppressed until exact option identity is known.
Partial mechanics such as Locations, Secrets, generated entities, aura, Destroy, Silence, Transform, and Imbue can still contribute useful pre-run posture without claiming a full action tree.

Warning-only mechanics such as Dredge, Tradeable, Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Rewind, Herald, and Shatter remain visible and non-blocking by design. Their absence from runtime rows is a safety boundary, not a package-invalidating failure.

Unknown future mechanics still degrade safely. `future_keyword` falls back to registered=false, `warning_only`, `report-only`, and `unregistered_mechanic_runtime_surface`, which preserves the any-valid-deck promise.
hearthstone_semantic_assessment: Battlecry support is strong. Static semantics detect it, the registry marks it direct, and targeting-aware claims can lower through `BeforeBattlecryTargetBonus` while generic play timing can lower through `BeforePlayCardBonus`.

Target behavior is split correctly. Exact targeting claims are runtime-lowerable, while the broader unresolved targeting class is represented by `generic_spell_target` warning-only. This is conservative but technically coherent.

Discover is strong but identity-gated. Static semantics detect it, the registry exposes `OnDiscoverCardBonus`, resolved option identity can emit `my_discover(...)` conditions, and unresolved choice identity is explicitly suppressed.
Choose One follows the same safety model as Discover. The mechanic is recognized and can lower to `OnChooseOneCardBonus` only when the chosen option is resolved.

Hero Power transforms are well covered for a pre-run generator. Static semantics infer Start of Game and hero-power-transform families, and runtime lowering routes to `BeforeUseHeroPowerBonus` when the transformed identity is known.

Weapons are direct and practical. The registry allows `BeforePhysicalAttackBonus`, `BeforePlayCardBonus`, and combo participation, which is enough for common Wild weapon-pressure and weapon-combo shells.
Locations are partial. The play card itself is visible and lowerable, but repeated activation and exact activation targeting remain warning-only through `location_activation`.
Secrets are partial. Secret cards and mulligan posture are represented, but hidden-information sequencing remains warning-only through `secret_timing`.
Generated entities are partial. Exact generated identity can be represented when linked, but random pools remain warning-only through `generated_entity_random_pool`.

Aura is partial but correctly scoped. Persistent board-value posture is representable through `OnBoardBonus` and `BeforePlayCardBonus`, while continuous stacked board-state math is intentionally not treated as a dedicated runtime planner.

Discard is direct enough for pre-run use. The enabler timing can lower to `BeforePlayCardBonus`, even though specific discard outcomes still remain in the card rules rather than HSConfig state simulation.

Destroy, Silence, and Transform are partial. Battlecry-target variants and explicit source-backed targeting can lower, but generic spell-target versions and random outcomes remain outside safe default lowering.
Dredge and Tradeable are correctly warning-only. Both are alternate decision surfaces without a documented normal-path VisionAI choice block, so report-only handling is the right boundary.

Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Rewind, Herald, and Shatter are explicitly covered as known mechanics rather than unknown drift. Today they remain warning-only because their signature behavior depends on prior-turn state, deck-construction crossover, build-and-launch state, temporal replay, card-specific scaling, or conditional frozen-target semantics.
Imbue is partial and sensibly placed. The current skill can represent Hero Power posture and upgraded-hero-power pressure without pretending it owns exact upgrade-state tracking.
Unknown future mechanics are handled safely but not richly. They stay visible in drift reporting and operator summaries without emitting runtime rows until a documented surface is added.
slimness_assessment: The current design stays lean because mechanic breadth is mostly handled by one registry plus drift reporting, not by expanding runtime write scope.
Modern mechanic coverage did not drag HSTuner, replay parsing, winrate logic, or post-run tuning into the repo. The implementation remains inside the intended pre-run HSConfig boundary.

Warning-only coverage is a slim solution. Adding visibility for Rewind, Herald, Shatter, Dredge, Tradeable, Kindred, Tourist, and Starship is cheaper and safer than inventing speculative runtime rows.
The routing layer is disciplined. Only documented VisionAI blocks are emitted, and unsupported explicit blocks or unknown mechanics are suppressed with explicit reasons.
The current repo is efficient enough for maintenance because future mechanic drift can usually be handled with a small registry row and a focused test instead of a broad architecture change.
recommended_next_action: Add one small supplemental visibility fixture or matrix check centered on Secret-heavy, Location-heavy, and Dredge or Tradeable cards, so the current warning-only and partial boundaries stay live against Wild drift without broadening runtime lowering.
confidence: high - the verdict is supported by the current mechanic registry, the runtime surface router, the static semantic and drift detectors, the operator no-block contract, and 78 passing targeted tests on 2026-07-11
